PennGlobal: PMR203
Period: VS 1351 śaka 1216
Location: Būdhērā
King: Gaṇapati
Language: Sanskrit
Script: Nagari
Text: Prose 
Gist: The first half refers to the ruler Gaṇapati. 
	The second half of the inscription introduces Pradgān Raviha of Jatuhaṭṭa,
 	his son MudhaIsIha and the latter's two sons, Harirāja and Ayarāja, 
 	both of whom lost their lives in battle fighting an unnamed enemy.  
	The Pillar was erected in memory of their death.
Published reference: Trivedi (1989), no. 203.


Text{1}

1. [saṃ]vat 1351 śāke{2} 1[21]6 || svasti śrīkī-
2. rttidugre(rge) samastarāja(jā)valīsamalaṃkṛtapa[rmaṃ(rama)]-
3. [bha]ṭārka(ṭṭāraka)[paḍi]maraja{3} [śrīga]ṇapatimahāpradhāna-
4. deuva . . {4}vyāpā[raṃ] karoti | jauhaṭṭipradhāna{5}-
5. ravija[patnī]dinasutamudhaisīha{6} pu-
6. [tra]ha[ri]rājajairā[ju]dauhatu{7} | laghuputratri[dhau]
7. . . . . {8}ndi[supu]tre[ṇa] [ja]marāyaṇa{9} ni[ve]hede[yaṃ(yam)]{10} ||

----------------------------------------

{1} From plate facing p.165 in Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXIII.
{2} The consonant of the penultimate sibilant is palatal and not dental, as used in samasta in the next
	line.
{3} Read paramarāja.
{4} The two akṣaras which are lost here may have been mudrā, as suggested by Sircar.
{5} As read by Sircar, according to whom, the first of these words is the Sanskrit Jatuhaṭṭīya. But all
	the letters here are mutilated, and the last two appear as sāta.
{6} All these letters are either mutilated or lost, and are given here as tentatively read by Sircar.
{7} Reading uncertain.
{8} Four syllables are lost here.
{9} Probably we have to read yēṇa, to be restored to Yamarājēna.
{10} As read by Sircar, who amended them to niravāhit ēyam. But some of the letters are misformed
	 and some others are lost.
